decisions.statement: A peripheral asks alanwalton.com who a person is, and asks no provider itself.
No Better Auth is reached from here, so a peripheral holds no provider secret.
A code is an EdDSA JWT naming the one origin that code is for.
A code lives thirty seconds, and a code living longer than sixty is refused.
No record is kept of a code spent, so an unexpired code handed back twice is taken twice.
A site signs its session cookie with a key of its own.
A session cookie carries the contributor slug and an issued-at, and nothing else.
A return path is a path of the peripheral's own, and a code sends nobody off-site.
A code that will not read sends the person back to the start of the handover, signing nobody in.

definition: the sign-in a peripheral borrows from alanwalton.com, taken as a code and kept as its own cookie
